clue.text: Lover about to seduce one in charge of the screamers

definitions.text: one in charge of the screamers

indicators.note: the lover's word goes round the outside of the seduction word, so 'about' means surrounding

parts.note: a suitor is a man who woos, a lover
to bed someone is to seduce them

explanation.surface: A lover is on the point of seducing someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screamers' is slang for exclamation marks, and the person who edits copy decides how many survive.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper copy editor polices punctuation, including the exclamation marks that journalists call screamers.

clue.text: Workers given stick

definitions.meaning: the employees of an organisation collectively

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the people employed by a firm and a long pole or rod carried in the hand.

clue.text: Steal away: snatch up non-touching item

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' tells you to read the whole run of letters from bottom to top

parts.note: to elope is to steal away secretly to marry
to grab is to snatch

explanation.surface: Instructions to slip away after grabbing something.
explanation.walkthrough: ELOPE then GRAB, in the clue's order, are read upwards all together as one string. The definition plays on the idiom 'I wouldn't touch it with a bargepole'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom of refusing to touch something even with a long punt pole makes it the item of non-contact.

clue.text: Many politicians wish they were so gorgeous

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, so a crossword 'many'
every politician wants to be electable, able to win votes

explanation.surface: Lots of politicians wish they were good-looking.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests vanity, but 'so' points to being electable, with D in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Delectable describes something delightful or very attractive, a close synonym for gorgeous.

clue.text: Time in firm completed

indicators.note: the time abbreviation is placed inside the word for firm

parts.note: tough meat is firm, resistant
HR is the abbreviation for hour, a unit of time

explanation.surface: A period spent at a company has come to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time' looks like it wants T, but here it is HR (hour) going into TOUGH.
explanation.definitionFit: Through can mean finished, as in 'I am through with this job'.

clue.text: As more than one spoke about end of rhetoric, progressive

indicators.note: the spoke-like word goes round the final letter of the speechmaking word

parts.note: spokes in a wheel are arranged radially, fanning out from a hub

indicators.note: 'end of' picks the last letter of the word it governs

explanation.surface: A forward-looking orator talks about finishing with rhetoric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoke' looks like the past tense of speak, fitting rhetoric, but it is the wheel part; several spokes together are radial. C, the last letter of 'rhetoric', goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A radical in politics is a progressive reformer seeking fundamental change.

clue.text: Vessel, one hollowed out

parts.note: a can is a container, a vessel for liquid

indicators.note: hollowing a word removes its insides, leaving just the outer letters

explanation.surface: A boat made from a trunk scooped out by hand.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole the clue describes a dugout, a log hollowed out to make a boat; CAN plus the outer letters of 'one' builds it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dugout boat is literally a log hollowed out, and it is a small vessel paddled by hand.

clue.text: 101 under 99?

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100, so 101 splits as C and one
C is the Roman numeral for 100, so 101 splits as C and one

explanation.surface: A number puzzle: 101 sits below 99.
explanation.walkthrough: A 99 is a British ice cream with a chocolate Flake stuck in it, and it is served on a wafer holder below.
explanation.definitionFit: A '99' ice cream sits on top of its wafer holder, so the holder is literally under the 99.

clue.text: Welsh town requests orderly for hospital

parts.note: neat means orderly, tidy

explanation.surface: A Welsh town asks for a hospital orderly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orderly' reads as a hospital porter, but it is the adjective meaning tidy. NEATH is a town in south Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Neath is a market town in south Wales, near Swansea.

clue.text: Gregarious old dog enters race

parts.note: ex- means former, old

indicators.note: the dog's name goes inside the race abbreviation

parts.note: TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
Rover is the stock name for a dog

explanation.surface: A sociable elderly dog joins a race.
explanation.definitionFit: An extrovert is an outgoing, sociable person who enjoys company.

clue.text: Taxing time when Ford loses leadership at fifty

indicators.note: losing its leader means dropping the first letter of the car's name

parts.note: the Capri was a Ford car model
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A man called Ford is ousted as leader at fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ford' looks like a person (Harrison or Gerald), but it is the car maker, giving the Ford Capri. The UK tax year begins in April.
explanation.definitionFit: The British tax year begins on 6 April, so this month is the season of tax returns.

clue.text: Regular payment about due cut off and made this, due to lack of work?

definitions.text: this, due to lack of work?

indicators.note: 'about' signals that the letters are moved around into a new order

parts.note: rent is a regular payment for accommodation

indicators.note: cutting off the word 'due' loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone laid off because there was no work.
explanation.walkthrough: RENT, DU ('due' cut off) and AND are rearranged, signalled by 'about'. 'Made this' means 'made the answer', so the clue's 'this' stands for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers are made redundant when their jobs are cut because there is not enough work.

clue.text: Dissenting Christians cheer wildly, entering something warm, cold and hot

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the warm thing

parts.note: fur is a warm covering

indicators.note: wildly signals that the letters of the word are thrown into disorder

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: Christian dissenters cheer wildly, wrapped against warm and cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' reorders the five letters of the cheering word; 'something warm' is a fur coat or wrap, and 'cold and hot' are the tap letters added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A Free Church is a Protestant church independent of the state, whose members are nonconformists or dissenters.

clue.text: Mum has binoculars — scram!

parts.note: 'mum' means silent, as does the call 'sh'
OO looks like a pair of lenses side by side

explanation.surface: Mother has a pair of field glasses and tells someone to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like a mother, but it is silence, shown as SH.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoo is an exclamation used to drive someone away, an order to go away.

clue.text: Hurried dismissal is going through

parts.note: ran means hurried
a sacking is a dismissal from a job

explanation.surface: A rushed dismissal is in progress.
explanation.definitionFit: Ransacking a place means searching it thoroughly and roughly, going through everything.

clue.text: Stand connects to machine part

indicators.note: 'part' says only a section of the words is taken, a run of letters within them

explanation.surface: A support links up with a part of a machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand' looks like a mechanical support, but it is the verb meaning tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: To stomach something is to tolerate it, just as you might say you cannot stand it.

clue.text: Logical thinker bags century in the test

indicators.note: the Star Trek character's name holds the other letters inside

parts.note: Mr Spock of Star Trek is famously ruled by logic

indicators.note: the century letter goes inside the word 'the'

parts.note: C is 100, a century

explanation.surface: A rational person scores a hundred in the exam.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes into THE to make TCHE, and SPOCK 'bags' that, SPO-TCHE-CK. 'century' and 'test' make it sound like cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot check is a random inspection, a test carried out without warning.

clue.text: Horror actor swallows a smoke which is green

indicators.note: the actor's name goes round the other letters, taking them in

parts.note: Christopher Lee starred in many Hammer horror films
fag is British slang for a cigarette, a smoke

explanation.surface: A horror film star draws on a cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: Christopher Lee was the Hammer horror star, and 'fag' is British slang for a cigarette; 'green' here is the noun, greenery.
explanation.definitionFit: Leafage is foliage, the greenery of plants.

clue.text: Great bloke, a tragic Greek admitting kiss

indicators.note: the Greek lover's name lets the kiss symbol into it

parts.note: Leander drowned swimming the Hellespont to his lover Hero
X is the sign for a kiss

explanation.surface: A great guy is a doomed Greek who owns up to a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great' refers to Alexander the Great, the Macedonian conqueror.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander the Great was the Macedonian king whose epithet is Great.

clue.text: Bit of a coincidence proving a handful during parole, drunk

indicators.note: the handful goes inside the reworked letters
drunk suggests the letters are reeling into a new order

parts.note: V is five in Roman numerals, a hand's worth of fingers

explanation.surface: A drunken parolee proves difficult to manage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges PAROLE into OERLAP, and V goes inside it. 'Proving a handful' looks like a phrase about trouble, but 'a handful' is five, V.
explanation.definitionFit: An overlap is where two things coincide in part, a partial coincidence.

clue.text: See 23
Observe little change in cricket, perhaps

indicators.note: the coin letter goes inside the creature

parts.note: a cricket is one example of an insect
P is a penny, a small coin

explanation.surface: Watch for a small adjustment in a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cricket' wants to be the game but it is the insect, as 'perhaps' warns.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect is to look carefully at, to observe closely.

clue.text: Unsophisticated woman's indulgent session eating all food available, but no starters

indicators.note: the first letters of both pieces are dropped, the starters of a meal removed
the binge word swallows the food list

parts.note: a binge is an indulgent bout
a menu lists all the food on offer

explanation.surface: A naive woman's binge takes in the whole menu, skipping starters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no starters' plays on a meal skipping its first course: it drops the opening letter of each of the two words, after the food list goes inside the binge.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingenue is an innocent, naive young woman, especially as a stage role.

clue.text: Male spy left unseen

indicators.note: something unseen is missing, so the letter is taken out

parts.note: to clock is slang for to spot or spy

explanation.surface: A male spy has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spy' looks like a secret agent, but it is the verb, CLOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: A cock is a male bird, particularly the male of the domestic fowl.

clue.text: French dish in rise of 1%

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise reads the run of letters upwards

parts.note: 1% written out is 'one per cent', and the letters EPERC run through its middle

explanation.surface: A French dish goes up by one percent.
explanation.walkthrough: Write 1% out in words: inside ONE PER CENT sits the run EPERC, and 'rise of' reads it upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A crepe is a thin French pancake, a dish of France.

clue.text: Transport for tutor at RADA?

definitions.meaning: a horse-drawn passenger coach of old
a theatre coach; RADA is London's Royal Academy of Dramatic Art

explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old horse-drawn passenger vehicle and also, split up, a coach who trains stage actors.

clue.text: Domesticated elephant can start to giggle, given exciting exploratory operation

parts.note: an elephant is the type of something heavy
a domesticated animal is a pet
a tin is a can

indicators.note: 'start to' picks the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A tame elephant can make you giggle with an exciting operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'operation' sounds surgical, but the exploration is of a romantic, physical kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy petting is intimate fondling short of intercourse, an exciting exploration jokily dressed up as an operation.

clue.text: Queen Mary's bottom

parts.note: a royal's backside on the surface, but the Queen Mary is a liner, and its bottom is the ship's underside

explanation.surface: A rude reference to a queen's posterior.
explanation.definitionFit: The bottom of a ship such as the liner Queen Mary is the body of the vessel below the deck.

clue.text: One's innings brought to an end after this delivery

definitions.text: One's innings brought to an end after this delivery

parts.words: One's innings brought to an end after this delivery
parts.note: sounds like a batsman out to a ball in cricket, but 'innings' is one's lifetime, ended by a death sentence being carried out

explanation.surface: A batsman is dismissed by this ball.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an innings is a batsman's turn and a delivery is a ball; here the innings is a whole life.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrying out a death sentence ends a person's life, their innings in cricket slang.

clue.text: Large percentage of mankind I assume here?

definitions.text: Large percentage of mankind I assume here?

indicators.note: 'here' points to a spot inside the words just read, where the letters sit across the word breaks

explanation.surface: A guess about where much of humanity lives.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'mankind I assume'; read whole, the clue guesses where a large share of humanity lives, over a sixth of all people.
explanation.definitionFit: The country is home to a large share of humanity and is also the radio code word for the letter I.

clue.text: Ring king's given to little girl, literally

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king, in chess and cards
Nell is a girl's name, as in Little Nell of Dickens

explanation.surface: A ring from a king is handed to a young girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like jewellery, but it is the sound of a bell. Little Nell is the heroine of Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop, so 'literally' is a nod to literature.
explanation.definitionFit: A knell is the solemn ringing of a bell, especially for a death.

clue.text: Hat where information about novice homosexual bishop collected

indicators.note: the information word goes round the learner's letter

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
L is a learner, from the L-plate

indicators.note: the gay word gathers in the bishop's letters

parts.note: gay means homosexual
RR stands for Right Reverend, a bishop's title

explanation.surface: A hat shows where details about a gay trainee bishop were gathered.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information; RR is Right Reverend, the style of a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: A glengarry is a brimless Scottish cap with a crease down the crown and ribbons at the back.
